title: attribution/v1 audit-result
description: Output of an attribution audit over a time window: how many sessions were exactly attributed to a single task_run vs. unbound/mixed/orphaned, and whether the window is eligible for research use. See docs/protocols/attribution-v1.md. Two rules this schema alone cannot express, enforced instead as semantic checks in verify-fixtures.mjs: (1) `research_eligible` MUST be false if `violations` is non-empty (fail-closed, not advisory) -- see 'Rejected designs' for why this MUST is not softened to a warning. (2) when `sessions.measured` is 0, `tokens.exact_attributed`/`tokens.total_measured` MUST be null, never 0 (null-not-zero: 'nothing was measured' and 'zero tokens were measured' are different facts).

sessions.description: measured = total sessions observed in window. exactly_attributed = sessions cleanly resolved to exactly one task_run (the accounting principle this whole protocol exists to certify). The four lists are disjoint session_id lists explaining every session NOT in exactly_attributed -- their union's length plus exactly_attributed MUST equal measured (checked by verify-fixtures.mjs, not expressible as a JSON Schema constraint over sibling array lengths).

tokens.description: exact_attributed = total tokens from sessions.exactly_attributed sessions only. total_measured = total tokens across every measured session (exactly_attributed + unbound + mixed + orphan_usage + measurement_incomplete), still just a measured total -- NEVER a mixed-session apportionment (see docs/protocols/attribution-v1.md 'Rejected designs': splitting a mixed session's tokens by time ratio between its tasks is a fabrication this protocol forbids, not merely discourages). Both fields are null, not 0, when sessions.measured is 0.
